summary: Minot Peak lookout from 1929 (cabin or tower), 50 ft pole tower 1935, 40 ft timber tower 1959, destroyed about 1971; summit now has communication towers.

facts.design: Cabin (1929), then 50 ft pole tower with observation room (1935), then standard 40 ft timber tower with live-in cabin (1959)
facts.status_note: Last tower destroyed about 1971; the summit now holds communication towers.

access.note: The guide lists a Weyerhaeuser permit area (Aberdeen general access permit). A motorized access permit shortens the approach to about one mile, and the final mile is a gated road walked on foot.

visit.trail_note: About five miles from the Boy Scout camp on the P-100 line, or about one mile with a motorized access permit.

facts.agency: Washington State Division of Forestry / Department of Natural Resources

events.note: Cabin built (firetower.org); other histories say a tower was erected that year, citing the 22nd annual report of the Washington Forest Fire Association
George M. Landon, the earliest named lookout
August 1930 fire, believed started by berry pickers or campers, forced Landon to abandon his post

50 ft pole tower and observation room constructed
Aircraft Warning Service Station How 1-6 used existing state facilities and added a 12x20 garage; state kept the structures for fire detection afterward
Late-November storm with 72 mph gusts toppled the tower after an anchor gave way
Tower re-erected and put back in use
Ben Harner lookout for several years in the early 1950s, then Martha Depoe of Shelton; the source gives no exact years, so 1950 is an approximation
New standard 40 ft timber tower with live-in cabin replaced the earlier lookout

corrections.why: 213.4 m is about 700 ft and matches no tower height in the sources. The last tower, built in 1959, was a standard 40 ft timber tower (about 12.2 m). The 1935 pole tower was 50 ft (about 15.2 m). An NGS datasheet (PID SC1607, described 1953) gives the tower standing then, a wooden four-leg structure, as 57 ft (about 17.4 m); the sources do not say whether that was the 1935 or the 1946 tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firetower.org and firelookout.com describe a cabin built in 1929; the Forest Lookouts page and WillhiteWeb cite a 1929 annual report saying a tower was erected. The story says sources disagree on what the 1929 structure was, and gives the 1935 pole tower as the first described tower.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 213.4 is about 700 ft and matches no tower height in the sources. The record proposes 12.2 m for the 1959 40 ft tower. An NGS datasheet (PID SC1607, described 1953) gives the tower then standing as 57 ft (about 17.4 m), which the editor may want if the field is meant for that structure. The 1935 tower was 50 ft (15.2 m). The summit-today and access details come from WillhiteWeb's peakbagging page, which carries no date, so check current permit status before publishing. The permit route notes are from that one source. No photos were found.
